ET-M3-1.statement: Generation runs only from known sim scenes, with the initial state and asset hashes saved first; a scene-consistency check rejects injected mismatches.
ET-M3-1.candidate: a candidate is (i) a candidate manifest: the snapshot manifest's task id and version, seed, asset sha256s, cube half size and colour, and goal position; (ii) frames 0 to T of one recorded episode on that scene, rendered at 512 x 512 from the human render camera, frame 0 after restore_state and frame t after control step t; and (iii), for frame eligibility only, the joint positions and cube position that restore_state of the scene's saved initial state returns, the human render camera's centre (the translation column of the snapshot manifest's cam2world_gl), and the candidate's actions a_1 to a_T, a_t being the absolute pd_joint_pos target applied at control step t. An injection alters frames and the manifest, never (iii). No generator exists yet, so physics frames stand in for generated frames.
ET-M3-1.size_checkable_frames: The sightline is the segment from the camera's centre to the cube's initial centre. The arm's skeleton at a joint vector is arm_segments in the pinned src/vishwaroop/sim/so100_kinematics.py: line segments, without the links' thickness, from the base (world position (-0.725, 0, 0), yaw pi/2) through each joint origin of the mani_skill 3.0.1 SO-100 URDF chain in order to the fixed jaw's frame, then to the fixed jaw tip, and through the moving jaw's origin to its tip. Its clearance is the shortest distance from any skeleton segment to the sightline. Frame 0 is size-checkable when the clearance at the initial joint positions is more than 0.035 m; frame t >= 1 when frame t - 1 is and the clearance at a_t (all six values) is more than 0.035 m. So the size-checkable frames are frames 0 to n - 1, n between 0 and T + 1: the frames before the arm is first commanded near the sightline. The clearance is tested at the commanded targets only, not at the rendered arm, which lags them. Because the sightline ends at the cube's centre, a clearance above 0.035 m also keeps every skeleton segment more than 0.035 m from that centre. Both are geometric proxies; the pilot checks their premise in the simulator (stops 2 and 3). No image, mask or cube-area measurement enters this rule, so a resized, removed or duplicated cube cannot change which frames are size-checkable.
ET-M3-1.episode_kind: on even seeds the nominal scripted demo (VARIANTS['nominal']); on odd seeds an operator episode, m3-synth-lateral-miss and m3-synth-close-high alternating by seed, drawn as F2's rule in evals/M3-exit-tests.json
ET-M3-1.visibility: For a frame, r is its merged red area (the red components whose centroids lie within the merge radius of the largest one's centroid, under this protocol's pilot-set merge radius) divided by the snapshot render's merged cube area, compared unrounded. A frame shows the cube when r >= 0.02; shows no cube when r = 0; and its visibility is uncertain when 0 < r < 0.02. 0.02 is about 12 pixels of a cube of about 600 at 512 x 512. It is fixed here, not set by a pilot.
ET-M3-1.checker: deterministic, with no learned part, every check applied to every candidate: manifest: the candidate manifest's fields equal the snapshot's; frame_shape: every frame has the render's shape; first_frame: frame 0 equals the snapshot's saved render within the first-frame tolerance; cube_size: in every size-checkable frame, r is within the pilot-set size band [a_lo, a_hi], subject to 0.36 < a_lo and a_hi < 2.56 (protocol-2's size check, unchanged); cube_presence: the final frame T shows the cube (r >= 0.02), and a final frame that shows no cube or whose visibility is uncertain fails; extra_red: in every frame, no red component outside the merge radius has at least 0.25 x the snapshot render's cube area; goal_centroid: in every frame with at least the pilot's minimum count of green pixels (and at least one), the green centroid is within the goal-centroid distance of the snapshot's. There is no per-frame presence requirement and no upper area bound outside the size-checkable frames. A snapshot render with no cube fails cube_size and cube_presence. A candidate with no size-checkable frame (n = 0) gets no cube_size check and still gets cube_presence. For T = 15 planning-failure episodes every frame is size-checkable, so frame T meets both rules.
ET-M3-1.how_it_tells_missing_from_occluded: No single frame tells a hidden cube from a missing one: a cube held or covered by the gripper can show no pixels at all (in-sample, 40 frames in one episode). So the rule uses when a frame comes, not what it shows. (1) Before the arm is first commanded near the camera-to-cube sightline, nothing can hide the cube, so cube_size requires the whole cube at its size; a missing or uncertain cube there fails. (2) After that, the checker accepts a frame that shows no cube or is uncertain, without deciding which; a missing cube and an occluded one are treated alike there. (3) At the final frame the cube must be seen again (r >= 0.02). Uncertain visibility at T counts as not seen and fails: the checker needs positive evidence that the cube still exists at the end. The cost: a candidate whose cube is legitimately hidden at its last frame, or knocked off the table or out of view, is rejected, which the checker cannot tell from removal. 'Shows the cube' is only a red area of at least 0.02 x the reference; it does not check position or shape after the size-checkable frames.
ET-M3-1.tolerance_pilot: block 10 seeds 10920 to 10939, used for nothing else, with the episode_kind alternation. The masks (red: R > 120, G < 60, B < 60; green: G > 120, R < 80, B < 80; 8-connectivity) and the rule are protocol-1's: each tolerance is the pilot's observed extreme widened by 10% (upper extremes x 1.1, lower x 0.9). The size band takes r's extremes over size-checkable frames only, subject to 0.36 < a_lo and a_hi < 2.56; the merge radius, first-frame tolerance, goal-centroid distance and minimum green count are taken over every frame. No presence band is set. The pilot records each candidate's n, and at every frame the simulator's cube position and the sightline clearance of the simulator's actual joint positions. It evaluates every condition below and, if any holds, writes nothing to evals/, lists all that hold, and the owner is told before any control or injection is generated: (1) more than 2 of the 20 pilot candidates have no size-checkable frame t with 1 <= t <= T - 1; (2) in a size-checkable pilot frame the simulator's cube centre is more than 0.005 m from its initial position; (3) a size-checkable pilot frame's r is outside [0.95, 1.05]; (4) the widened size band is not inside its limits; (5) no pilot frame is size-checkable; (6) a snapshot render shows no cube or no goal; (7) a pilot candidate's final frame does not show the cube (r < 0.02); (8) the merge radius is 60 px or more, the smallest duplicate offset, so a duplicate could merge with the cube; (9) the goal-centroid distance is at least the smallest image displacement of a 0.03 m goal move on any pilot scene, over directions every 1 degree in xy, from the camera's projection, so a type-4 pixel shift could pass. A snapshot without an exposed render camera refuses the run, before any result is written. Otherwise the tolerances go to evals/M3-checker-tolerances-p3.json with protocol_version m3-protocol-3, and its sha256 is recorded in the status ledger before any control or injection is generated.

ET-M3-1.reported: rejections by type and by the check that caught each; every source candidate's own result; false rejections with their cause; the false-rejection count with its Wilson 95% interval; how often the size check runs (protocol-2's list); for every candidate its final-frame r, its longest run of frames with r < 0.02 and where it starts, and, from the simulator, its final cube position and whether that is on the table and projects inside the image (reporting only, not part of the rule); the number of candidates whose final frame is uncertain or shows no cube; the pilot's merge radius and goal-centroid distance against stops (8) and (9); each type-3 injection's seed, skipped seeds, step and T; what happens at n = 0 and when visibility is uncertain (above); the limits below; and a statement that controls are physics renders, so this does not estimate false rejection on generated frames (ET-M3-2 measures that)
ET-M3-1.risk_before_freezing: estimated, not measured. Controls: with no final-frame failure in 160 in-sample episodes, more than 3 of 60 failing is very unlikely (well under 1%). Sources are the binding risk: one failing source fails the test under the credit rule. A rate of 1 in 160 to 1 in 320 per episode would give about 17% to 31% that at least one of 60 sources fails cube_presence. The closest in-sample case (0.137, a lateral-miss) is about 7 times the 0.02 floor. Off-table or out-of-view endings are recorded but cannot be told from removal. Type 2 relies on extra_red alone (stop 8 guards the merge radius); type 4's pixel shift relies on the goal-centroid tolerance (stop 9 guards it).
ET-M3-1.limits: A cube that disappears after the size-checkable frames and reappears before the end is not caught by cube_presence, and a size error after those frames is not caught by cube_size; an enlarged cube is caught only in size-checkable frames. ET-M3-1 shows that the checker catches a removal that persists to the end, a duplicate, and a resize that starts before the arm approaches. ET-M3-2 has to judge presence and size in the frames between.
